answer: Crack a walnut no shortcut can open: each epoch gives every account a unique verifiable-delay puzzle taking real minutes to solve, so one operator cannot crack many accounts in time. Then split the population into random islands: each island's members must jointly confirm a shared public event within a short window, and islands whose answers arrive in lockstep are quarantined as one operator's farm. Finally, charge a tiny copper fee per answer that is burned, not refunded, so mass submissions cost real money while honest users pay almost nothing.
